expectations.text: Frames the issue: civil vs criminal, substantive vs procedural, area of law
expectations.evidence: Section 1 'Frame the issue (Nolo's four steps, Ch. 3)': 'Civil, mainly' plus 'A possible criminal side'; separate 'Substantive issues' and 'Procedural issues' bullets; state vs federal; Step 2 'Area(s) of law' (contracts/commercial, consumer, tort/criminal, civil procedure). Matches SKILL.md's four-step framing.

expectations.text: Uses the Cartwheel method or keyword brainstorming
expectations.evidence: Section 2 'Search terms (Cartwheel)' table uses exactly the skill's nine categories (major words, broader, narrower, synonyms, antonyms, closely related, procedural, agencies, long shots) plus Boolean queries; the 'runs out of patience at the index' quote matches the skill.

expectations.text: Points to secondary sources first (e.g. practice guides, Am. Jur., form books) then primary law
expectations.evidence: Section 3 'Start with secondary sources (Ch. 2 and 4)' before Section 4 'Primary law': Nolo.com/Everybody's Guide to Small Claims Court, NY practice guide or encyclopedia (NY Jurisprudence), UCC treatise; 'state-specific source is almost always best' matches the skill's state-encyclopedia note. Then NY UCC, federal regs, small claims acts, cases.

expectations.text: Mentions checking that law is still good (Shepardize/KeyCite or updates/pocket parts)
expectations.evidence: Section 5 'Validate everything (Ch. 8)': 'check the pocket part, or the online update', 'Shepardize or KeyCite statutes', 'run any case... through Shepard's or KeyCite', free at county/law school library. Consistent with skill Ch 8.

expectations.text: Mentions small claims court and/or when to hire a lawyer; notes it's not legal advice
expectations.evidence: Header: 'This is legal information, not legal advice.' Sections 4C, 6 cover NY small claims court; Section 8 'When to involve a lawyer' (pattern of scams, legal aid, limited-scope help).
